The operative context establishes that authorized users can create and modify penalty records before invoice finalization, penalties are calculated based on configured rules, and disputes can be tracked through multiple states. The exception clarifies that modifications are only permitted before finalization. A critical gap exists regarding a potential early-cancellation tolerance window that may have been removed from documentation. The following 10 test cases cover penalty creation, modification restrictions, dispute tracking, calculation basis, and invoice integration, while avoiding unsupported claims about the missing tolerance window.
resolvedOperativeContext: Users can submit disputes for penalties with tracked status (Open, Under Review, Approved, Rejected) || ## 9.5.1 The system shall allow authorized users to create penalty records. || Authorized users can create and modify penalty records before invoice finalization
resolvedExceptions: Authorized users can modify penalty records only before invoice finalization
resolvedConflictsOrObsolete: Earlier lifecycle guidance may have included a tolerance window for early cancellation that would waive penalties, but this exemption language appears to be missing from current documentation
resolutionNotes: R97b defines the penalty application rule with multiple operational requirements spanning late returns, damage incidents, penalty management, and dispute resolution. PRIMARY evidence (E1–E12) establishes core behaviors: penalties are calculated based on configured rules, associated with rent records, included in invoices, and subject to authorized modification before finalization. A critical gap exists regarding a potential early-cancellation tolerance window that may have been removed from documentation without explicit decision (E1, E5). The exact penalty calculation formula and configurable rule parameters remain undefined (E6, E9). Audit logging requirements are specified but implementation details around user-identity handling in logs need clarification (E3). CONTEXT evidence (E13) refines the lateness threshold definition. Implementation I94b addresses late return penalty calculation. The requirement is operationally sound for standard penalty application but carries unresolved ambiguities around grace periods and rule finalization that should be resolved before test generation."
